thread:
alex: Heads-up — getting a spike in tail token latency (~99.9th) for /chat/large on prod-us-east-1 (GPU pool: mig-split-4). Dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/route-kpi?panel=token-breakdown

maya: I pulled the flamegraphs. Looks like kernel-selector fell back to a generic GEMM path for a subset of steps, and batching collapsed into lots of tiny batches between 4-12 tokens. SM occupancy vs token index shows weird oscillation. Link to profile: https://perf.redwood/team/algo/1802004321-profile

sam: Noted. Could be KV cache prefetch thrash + small-batch penalty. When KV hits are <75% we see the runtime re-materialize more states and that triggers different kernel paths. Any logs?

alex: Pasted the tail of the runtime log (sanitized):
```
[2027-02-11T14:18:42Z] route=/chat/large req=0x7f9 kernel_selector: fallback_generic_gemm chosen (ctx_len=4096 seq=128)
[2027-02-11T14:18:42Z] batching: batch_sizes=[1,2,1,1,3,1,...] avg=2.1
[2027-02-11T14:18:43Z] kvcache: miss_ratio=0.42 prefetch_queue=12
[2027-02-11T14:18:44Z] mig: slice_alloc=3 cross_queue_wait=18ms
```

maya: That `slice_alloc=3 cross_queue_wait=18ms` is telling — MIG scheduling is rebalancing and we're paying cross-slice synchronization. The VMEM pressure (VRAM used / capacity) for the node hits ~94% at the same time.

lee: If VRAM is that high we also hit the fallback quantized path in some layers which may use different kernels with worse latency on small batches. Do we know which layers flip?

maya: From the profile: attention and ffwd layers 5-8 show kernel changes. The selector switched from `fast_attn_epic` to `attn_fallback_v2` around step 62 for these requests.

sam: Mitigation ideas: 1) bump dynamic batcher hold_time from 8ms -> 18ms for this route to reduce tiny batches; 2) add KV prefetch hint when route expects long contexts so we warm the cache sooner; 3) schedule /chat/large to non-MIG nodes when expected context > 2k. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

alex: I like 1+2 as quick canary. 3 requires infra SLA review but put it in backlog. Can we test 1) in canary and measure token-level breakdown?

toni-bot: Perf run scheduled: job=canary-dyn-batcher-1802004321 user=alex start=2027-02-11T14:30:00Z targets=[/chat/large] config={"hold_time_ms":18}

maya: Ran the canary locally against a replay of the bad traffic. Results look promising: 99.9th latency down from 2.4s -> 1.1s, avg unchanged. SM occupancy smoothed out (no oscillation), VRAM peak reduced ~6%. KV miss ratio moved from 0.42 -> 0.28.

sam: Nice. What about throughput impact? Any regression on p50/p90 for other routes due to holding batches longer?

maya: Measured per-route KPIs for a 10-minute window: /chat/large p50+p90 stable, consumer routes (shorter contexts) +1% latency p90 under load, throughput unchanged. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/perf/1802004321-canary-summary

lee: We should also add a kernel selection metric to the token breakdown dashboard (show fraction of tokens served by fallback kernels vs optimized kernels). That will make regressions visible earlier.

alex: Agreed. Action items:
- maya: roll canary to prod for next 30m, monitor token-level breakdown and SM occupancy (owner: maya)
- sam: add KV prefetch hint flag to route config and stage behind a toggle (owner: sam)
- lee: add kernel-selection fraction to dashboards + alert when fallback fraction > 5% (owner: lee)
- alex: coordinate infra if we need non-MIG capacity (owner: alex)

maya: I'll post a short summary in #eng-runtime once prod canary completes. :thumbsup:
